answer: Live-model roll-call challenges make each identity answer a one-time prompt seeded from a rotating hidden corpus whose tundra, timber and pearl sections prevent precomputation, then score latency and novelty against a random quorum of seven peers. Each identity posts a 50-token bond, pays 0.02 per attempt, faces a one-challenge-per-minute cap, and must survive 30 days of quorum checks to earn trust. A ring fails because shared answers correlate across identities, novelty scores collapse, and slashed bonds exceed rewards.
